title: CryptoServe Census: cryptographic dependency adoption across eleven public package registries
description:
Raw output from the CryptoServe Cryptographic Census: how many packages in each public registry depend on a catalogued cryptographic library, and how those dependencies split across weak, modern and post-quantum tiers.

This deposit archives the repository at a tag, and the repository holds more than one dataset. Each directory under datasets/ is an independent, immutable release with its own collection date, its own MANIFEST.json and its own SHA-256 per file. Cite the dated dataset you actually used, not this record as a whole. Datasets included at this tag:

  • datasets/2026-08-03 (raw+aggregate): 2,170,994 packages listed across 11 ecosystems, at least 37,242 of which were not read; 65,686 matched a catalogued cryptographic library. Of those, 12,465 are counted as depending on a library the catalogue classes as weak and 353 as declaring a catalogued post-quantum library. Published with per-package output for the matched packages, one file per ecosystem. Defects measured after publication are recorded in errata/2026-08-03.json; read it before quoting a figure.
  • datasets/2026-03-18 (aggregate-only): 2,809,479 packages listed across 11 ecosystems, 108,145 depending on a catalogued cryptographic library. Its raw per-package output does not exist and cannot be reconstructed; the aggregate survived because it was committed. Two ecosystem rows are annotated in place as known-wrong, both understating, and are not corrected retroactively.

Read the denominator before quoting a percentage. The scanned totals count packages listed, including packages that could not be read, not packages using cryptography. Every share published by this project is over the subset that matched a catalogued library. The March 2026 and August 2026 datasets are not comparable: the instrument changed between the two runs and the March raw output no longer exists, so no change over time can be read from them.

The August run listed fewer packages than March. That is not a regression: the March run enumerated more while classifying two ecosystems wrongly, and the current pipeline refuses to publish an ecosystem that enumerated implausibly little or matched nothing at all.

A published dataset is never rewritten. CI rejects any change that modifies or deletes a file under an existing dataset directory, and a correction is published as a new dated dataset that supersedes the old one and says so. That is the property this DOI depends on. A defect measured after publication is recorded in an errata file outside the dataset directory, so the deposited bytes do not change.
